source.exact_written_readback: For \(d=2,3,4,7,9,11,13,15,16\), sufficient \(L\)-onsets for \(P_d\) are respectively \(223,263,320,450,620,850,1300,2200,4000\). The first five coefficients are \(1,14,145,1412,13985\). Take the maximum of these branches, the positive sign, the local linear bound and the pointwise analytic bound below. At the earlier onset \(L=45\) one can use the whole-ray margin \(1+9/L\), versus \(1+14/L\) from 47.2. At fixed margin .5 use 37.77 instead of the later 39.38 needed by the .9 row. The \(1+13/L+100/L^2\) profile is better than \(1+14/L\) before their exact crossover \(L=100\), on their overlap. Constant normalized margins \(>1\) are not asserted on whole rays: the same log-integral expansions below with exponential π errors give limiting normalized gap 1.

their full matched domains: the ratio test is the same (K L^2e^{-L/8})

the first three matched domains is in ((40,41)) in log scale, and with
.3 for the weighted matched domain it is in ((35,36)).

respective original onsets. spectral_repair.py checks both brackets and the
earliest comparisons with directed arithmetic. Keep the polynomial branches
where they win; there is no assertion that the early extension of the power
branch beats them everywhere.
